context.resurgence_note: National incidence 45 / 1,000 (FY2023-24), then resurged to 76 (FY2024-25); severe cases rose 50% (1,316 -> 1,969) and deaths 23% (51 -> 67). ~15 districts carry ~87% of the burden.
context.surveillance_gap: the national malaria programme's own report names the gap this tool fills: "Lack of more granular data (cell, village, and individual level) to inform targeted interventions" and inadequate decentralized data use for timely response.
context.source: MOPDD Malaria & NTD Annual Report FY2023-24 (primary) + national weekly Public Health Bulletins.

climate.note: Rainfall leads malaria cases by ~8 weeks (documented in Rwanda).

suggestions.why: Flagged HIGH (+33% vs baseline, z=3.0). Verify reporting + eLMIS stock, then CHW surge in its hotspot sectors.
Gicumbi rose +4% year-on-year (also Nyagatare, Muhanga). Persistent rises despite prevention need a risk-factor investigation (national programme recommendation).

suggestions.action: Time the next prevention round to the rains
suggestions.why: The next major rainfall peak is ~epi-week 14 (~26 weeks away). Because rain leads cases by ~8 weeks, plan the next IRS/LLIN round to finish before then; the imminent short-rains rise is already in this week's alerts.
Nationally severe cases rose ~50%% and deaths ~23%% (report), alongside confirmed artemisinin partial resistance - sustain the MFT rollout and severe-case/death audits.
